question: Across the twelve calendar months of 2025, compute the Pearson correlation between monthly cancellation rate and average Delivered-order delivery time using SQL's CORR() function. Monthly cancellation rate = cancelled orders divided by all orders. Average delivery time = mean of delivery_time_min for Delivered orders with a non-null delivery duration only. Report the correlation coefficient, the number of months used, and whether that correlation alone supports a causal claim.

action.query:
SELECT 
  d.MONTH_NAME,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.ORDER_ID) AS total_orders,
  SUM(CASE WHEN o.IS_CANCELLED THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_orders,
  SUM(CASE WHEN o.IS_DELIVERED THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered_orders,
  AVG(CASE WHEN o.IS_DELIVERED AND o.DELIVERY_TIME_MIN IS NOT NULL THEN o.DELIVERY_TIME_MIN END) AS avg_delivery_time_min,
  (SUM(CASE WHEN o.IS_CANCELLED THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT o.ORDER_ID)) AS cancellation_rate
FROM ZOMATO_DLR.CORE.FACT_ORDER o
JOIN ZOMATO_DLR.CORE.DIM_DATE d ON o.ORDER_DATE = d.DATE_DAY
WHERE o.ORDER_DATE >= '2025-01-01' AND o.ORDER_DATE < '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY d.MONTH, d.MONTH_NAME
ORDER BY d.MONTH;

SELECT CORR(cancellation_rate, avg_delivery_time_min) AS pearson_corr
FROM (
  SELECT 
    d.MONTH_NAME,
    (SUM(CASE WHEN o.IS_CANCELLED THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT o.ORDER_ID)) AS cancellation_rate,
    AVG(CASE WHEN o.IS_DELIVERED AND o.DELIVERY_TIME_MIN IS NOT NULL THEN o.DELIVERY_TIME_MIN END) AS avg_delivery_time_min
  FROM ZOMATO_DLR.CORE.FACT_ORDER o
  JOIN ZOMATO_DLR.CORE.DIM_DATE d ON o.ORDER_DATE = d.DATE_DAY
  WHERE o.ORDER_DATE >= '2025-01-01' AND o.ORDER_DATE < '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY d.MONTH, d.MONTH_NAME
);

action.metrics: Pearson correlation coefficient, number of months, interpretation of causality
action.answer: The Pearson correlation coefficient between monthly cancellation rate and average delivered-order delivery time across the twelve calendar months of 2025 is -0.01999787909651581. This calculation used all 12 months in 2025. The correlation is very close to zero, indicating almost no linear relationship between the two variables at the monthly level. Correlation alone does not support a causal claim; it only measures the strength and direction of a linear association. Additional analysis and business context would be required to establish causality.
